newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech NPF says to reduce stake in NHut to minority.
newsitem.headline: Czech NPF says to reduce stake in NHut to minority.

text.p: The Czech National Property Fund (NPF) said on Friday that it will reduce its stake in steel mill Nova Hut a.s. to a minority share within three months.

NPF Chairman Roman Ceska told Reuters that the move, which will see the state privatisation agency's stake fall from a current 67.5 percent to 49 percent, was part of an agreement with the International Finance Corp (IFC) and its $250 million financing of the construction of a mini-mill at the plant.
Under the plan, the NPF will transfer an 18.5 percent stake in Nova Hut to banks Komercni Banka and CSFB, which will hold the shares until their sale.
Komercni Banka CEO Richard Salzmann said his bank expected to place the shares it will hold on the stock market, and not seel them as a package.
He did not specify how many shares Komercni would hold.

Earlier on Friday, the IFC signed a $75 million, 12-year loan agreement with the Czech steel maker as part of a $250 million credit package to help finance the construction of a hot-rolled coil mill at Nova Hut.
Construction of the mill is being managed by U.S.-based ICF Kaiser International.
The other part of the $250 million package comes in the form of a 10-year syndicated loan with 17 international banks, also signed on Friday.
Czech Komercni Banka also said it had been mandated on Friday by Nova Hut to arrange a 2.7 billion crown, 11-year syndicated loan for further financing on the project.

The total $650 million project is to completed by the year 2000, and will allow Nova hut to compete internationally as one of the low-cost steel producers of flat rather than long steel products which it traditionally had produced.
